Halcyon Threshold

Contributing to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Mission

Halcyon Threshold is an independent, small-team effort focused on practical preparedness for advanced AI. We believe superintelligence could be the best thing that ever happened to the world — if we get the transition right. That means better information, clearer coordination, and more reliable assessment of what’s actually happening in frontier development.

We work transparently and publish everything we can.

Current Work

Frontier Monitor v0

An open, human-curated tracker of frontier model releases, announced compute, and publicly available safety evaluations. Goal: make it easy for researchers, journalists and policymakers to see trends without relying on press releases alone.

Status: data collection in progress. First public table expected early December 2026.

Contact us to contribute data or suggest a metric.

Principles

  • Evidence over rhetoric.
  • Independence from labs and funders.
  • Concrete output first, narrative second.
  • Open by default.

Contact

Morgan Hale — Founder
morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
halcyonthreshold.org

© 2026 Halcyon Threshold. Opinions are our own.

# Rapid Grant Proposal — Emberfall Fund
Applicant: Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold
Date: 16 November 2026
Amount requested: $18,000 over 3 months

## What we will do
Build Frontier Monitor v0: an open, human-curated tracker of frontier model releases, announced compute, and publicly available safety evaluations. The first public release will be a sortable table with 24 months of historical data and a methodology note explaining how numbers are sourced and verified.

Deliverables
1. Public dataset (CSV + JSON) updated weekly, with source links for every entry.
2. Static site section with the table and change log.
3. One-page methodology document, peer-reviewed by two external reviewers.
4. Short write-up on gaps in public data and recommendations for labs and journalists.

Why now
Public information about frontier development is fragmented across press releases, conference papers, and leaked benchmarks. That makes it hard for the rest of the ecosystem — researchers, civil society, and press — to form a shared picture. A minimal, reliable baseline reduces speculation and improves coordination.

## Why Halcyon Threshold
We are small, independent, and publish everything. We have no lab affiliations and take no funding from labs. Our first priority is verifiable outputs, not advocacy. The team currently is Morgan Hale (founder, full-time) plus part-time data analyst support.

## Budget
- Data analyst (Priya Raman, 5 hrs/week x 12 weeks @ $60/hr): $3,600
- Research assistant stipend for source verification (12 weeks @ $1,200/mo): $3,600
- Web hosting & tools (Pagewell Pro 6 months + data storage): $120
- Open review and copyediting: $1,000
- Contingency / data access fees: $1,680
- Founder time (unpaid, costed at 0 for this round)

Total requested: $18,000

We will track spend publicly in a simple ledger linked from the site.

Applicant accountability
All work products will be released under CC-BY 4.0. Monthly updates will be posted to halcyonthreshold.org. Final report due 15 February 2027.

Contact
morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

# Frontier Monitor v0 — Plan

Goal: publish a minimal, verifiable dataset of frontier model releases with compute estimates and safety evaluations.

Data fields:
- date_announced
- model_name
- organization
- claimed_training_compute (FLOPs or parameter*token proxy)
- publicly_released (yes/no/partial)
- safety_eval summaries (AGI benchmarks, red team reports, public audits)

Sources: press releases, arXiv preprints, H100-equivalent estimates from Epoch AI, company transparency reports.

Process:
1. Priya validates sources and normalizes compute estimates.
2. Weekly update every Monday, changelog on site.
3. Methodology doc reviewed by external expert.

Risks: compute numbers are often not disclosed. We will explicitly mark estimates vs disclosed.

# Independence Statement

Halcyon Threshold is independent of AI labs, governments, and major funders.

We will not accept funding from labs that produce frontier models. We disclose all grants >$1,000 and all in-kind support.

We welcome corrections and publish our raw data.
